## My thinking for this year

My 10.1 mu is split roughly even — 5 mu for wheat-maize rotation on the better plot near the well, and the rest mixed in with another 5 mu doing the same rotation. Actually no, all of it is wheat-maize double cropping, that's the only way to make a living on this much land around here. Everyone in the village does it.

The wheat went in last October — I planted Jimai 22, same variety I've been using for four or five years now. Gives steady yield, doesn't lodge too bad. I put down about one bag (50 jin, so 25 kg) of compound fertilizer per mu as base, that's the 15-15-15 stuff from the agri-supply shop. Now in April the wheat is jointing, I'll topdress about 15 kg urea per mu before the next irrigation — the extension fellow said 12 is enough but I always add a bit extra because once you miss the window you can't fix it. Losing yield hurts more than wasting 30 yuan of urea.

For wheat irrigation I usually go three times — greenup in March (already did), jointing now, and grain filling in May. The well water isn't free, electricity for pumping runs maybe 40-50 yuan per mu per irrigation, but without water you get nothing on this sandy soil. Some of my neighbors only do two irrigations when electricity is expensive, but I'd rather pay than risk it.

After wheat harvest in early June, I've got maybe a week to get maize in. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, cost around 30 yuan per mu. No-till planter — I hire the custom operator from the next village, he does it in one pass through the wheat stubble for about 25 yuan per mu. I apply compound fertilizer at planting through the same machine, one bag per mu. Then one topdress of urea around V6-V8, maybe 10-12 kg. Maize around here is rainfed mostly, I only irrigate once if July-August is dry.

Pesticides — I spray herbicide on the wheat in spring, once, for broadleaf weeds. For maize I do a herbicide before emergence. Insecticide only if I see armyworm or borer damage, usually once on the maize. I don't spray on a schedule like the big farms, too expensive and I don't see the point if the pests aren't there.

Labor is just me and my wife mostly. Our son works in Shijiazhuang and sends money home but isn't here for the season. During wheat harvest I hire the combine (machine cost about 50 yuan per mu) and during maize harvest I do it with my wife and sometimes hire one or two day laborers for a couple days if it gets rushed.

My wheat yield last year was 450 kg/mu, maize was about 520 kg/mu. That's what I'm expecting this year if the weather is normal. Grain prices have been so-so — wheat around 2.5 yuan/kg at the grain station, maize 2.4. It's a thin margin after inputs but it's what we know.
